chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) spread out a parchment, and the first thing that met my eyes in it was: 'A son of a brother and a grandfather, the wealth is divided between them into two halves.' So I said, 'May I be your ransom, the judges with us do not rule for a son of a brother with a grandfather in anything.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed this book is written by Ali (peace be upon him) and dictated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided between a nephew and a grandfather according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the tension between the prevailing juristic opinion of the time, which excluded the nephew in favor of the grandfather, and the authoritative precedent set by the Prophet and Imam Ali. By presenting a written document (sahifa) dictated by the Prophet and penned by Ali, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the equal division of the estate, emphasizing the reliability of early written legal records in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle that specific prophetic instructions can override general judicial consensus.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, form Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> displayed a parchment, so the first of what faced me in it was a son of a brother (nephew) and a grandfather, then wealth (to be divided) between the two of them is two halves. So I said, ‘The judges with us are not judging with anything being for a son of the brother (nephew) with the grandfather’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This book is written by Ali<sup>asws</sup> and dictated by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “Once, abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, made a book available to the public. I found in it that the son of a brother and a grandfather share a legacy in equal shares. I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, the judges do not judge for the son of brothers with a grandfather anything.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘This book is in handwriting of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, as dictated to him by the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.”’
